mode_evidence: The text says 'we perceive both light and vision of forms' and that the light is perceived or not depending on which basis is attended to, for a whole night and day; the vocabulary of perceiving and seeing, with no mention of imagining or visualising.
onset_evidence: Nothing for someone who sees nothing: light and vision of forms are already occurring in diligent, keen, resolute meditation and the sutra is troubleshooting why they vanish. The Buddha says the same happened to him before awakening. Time scale for stable light: a whole night, a whole day, even a whole night and day.

conditions.duration_and_schedule: Light and forms sustained for a whole night and day once stable.
conditions.prerequisites: Diligent, keen and resolute practice; immersion (samadhi).

stages.label: light and vision of forms that vanish
stages.description: Appear while meditating but vanish before long when immersion falls away.

stages.label: light without forms or forms without light
stages.description: Depends on whether attention is on the basis of the light or of the forms.

stages.label: limited then limitless light and forms
stages.description: Scales with the limits of immersion.

what_to_do_with_light: Do not hold the light itself; diagnose and give up the eleven corruptions so immersion stays, then use the light and forms as indicators of immersion and develop immersion in three ways.
obstacles_and_fixes: Excessive energy (like gripping a quail too tightly)
Overly lax energy (like gripping a quail too loosely)
cautions: Each of the eleven states is a corruption of the mind that makes immersion fall away and the light vanish.
interpretation: Light and vision of forms are a result of immersion and a gauge of its extent: limited immersion gives limited light, limitless immersion limitless light.
practice_summary: When light or visions of forms appear and then vanish, the Buddha says look for what knocked immersion out: doubt, loss of focus, dullness, terror, elation, discomfort, too much or too little energy, longing, perception of diversity, or too much concentration on forms. Notice each as it arises and give it up, one after another. Energy is like holding a quail: too tight kills it, too loose lets it fly. Once the corruptions are cleared, light may be seen without forms or forms without light, depending on whether attention rests on the basis of the light or of the forms. The breadth of the light follows the breadth of your immersion, and it can last a night and a day.

key_passages.anchor: while meditating diligent, keen, and resolute, we perceive both light and vision of forms.
key_passages.paraphrase: Anuruddha reports perceiving both light and vision of forms in diligent meditation, which then vanish.
key_passages.quote: while meditating diligent, keen, and resolute, we perceive both light and vision of forms.

key_passages.anchor: When immersion falls away, the light and vision of forms vanish.
key_passages.paraphrase: The refrain behind all eleven diagnoses: loss of immersion makes the light vanish.
key_passages.quote: When immersion falls away, the light and vision of forms vanish.

key_passages.anchor: but focus on the basis of the light, then I perceive light and do not see forms.
key_passages.paraphrase: Attending to the basis of the light gives light without forms, and attending to the basis of forms gives forms without light.

key_passages.anchor: and with limitless vision I perceive limitless light and see limitless forms.
key_passages.paraphrase: Limited immersion gives limited light and forms; limitless immersion gives limitless light and forms.
key_passages.quote: and with limitless vision I perceive limitless light and see limitless forms.
